Use paired, category-stratified user bootstrap: record each model’s hit indicator on identical pinned candidates; independently resample 200 users with replacement within each category, using identical resampled indices across models/checkpoints. Compute each replicate’s difference as Δ* = ¼Σcategory mean(hit_new − hit_baseline); report the observed difference, category differences, and a 95% bootstrap interval, preferably with ≥10,000 replicates. Keep categories and candidates fixed. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on these trained models and candidate sets; it excludes training-seed and candidate-generation variability. One training seed cannot establish robustness across initialization or training order. Sampled HR can also reverse full-catalog model rankings, so improvement supports only the pinned benchmark. Sources: [paired bootstrap](https://aclanthology.org/www.mt-archive.info/EMNLP-2004-Koehn.pdf), [sampled recommendation metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

Repeated checkpoint/configuration selection creates optimism: an ordinary bootstrap interval around the validation winner is exploratory, not selection-adjusted evidence. Prespecify checkpoint frequency, maximum comparisons, stopping, and tie-breaking; for a fixed comparison family use simultaneous bootstrap bounds or multiplicity correction. These do not eliminate bias from unrecorded adaptive search; retain independent held-out evaluation for final assessment. [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).

Proposed compute rule: before searching, set a practically meaningful gain δ and full-catalog inference latency/memory ceiling; advance an expensive model only when its selection-adjusted lower improvement bound exceeds δ and projected remaining training, validation, diagnostics, simulator inference, and failures fit the remaining 43,200 GPU-seconds. Four concurrent slots consume summed GPU time. Benchmark full-catalog unseen-item inference for all 20 simulator users, including retrieval overhead. Prefer cheaper models when evidence is inconclusive; record final held-out inference separately, as prescribed.
